The agent claim lacks a matching admissible three-version oracle.; The intro commit (0a29578f) changed `DrcCompiler::alloc_array` (crates/cranelift/src/gc/enabled/drc.rs) to compute `num_gc_refs` for GC-ref-element arrays by reusing the `size` SSA value from `emit_array_size` (the array's total byte size including header) instead of the element count, packing this wrong value into the object's header reserved bits. Since the stored value is the byte size rather than the element count, the computed slice end overruns the object's real allocation — an out-of-bounds read matching the OutOfBoundsRead label (caught here as a Rust slice-bounds panic rather than raw memory corruption only because Rust's safe indexing interposes a bounds check before any unsafe byte access/pointer interpretation of the overrun region occurs) — reliably triggered whenever a Wasm module allocates and lets a GC-ref array get collected.

This requires actually executing the Cranelift-JIT-compiled `array.new_fixed` instruction; the equivalent host-API call (`ArrayRef::new_fixed`, as used e.g. by tests/all/gc.rs's drc_transitive_drop_nested_arrays_tree) goes through a separate, correct, native computation of num_gc_refs and does not reproduce the bug — explaining why the deterministic fast-path reproduction did not crash on any revision. - post_benign (04eee218, the fix): clean dealloc, no panic, exit 0 (`GC_DONE_NO_PANIC`) — object size 40 matching post_intro, confirming num_gc_refs is now correctly 3 (not the byte size).
